clue.text: Spider spinning on banks of Rhine showed signs of life

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so the outer letters of the word Rhine are taken
something spinning is turning round and round, so the letters of the word Spider are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spider whirls about on the riverside of the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: To respire is to breathe, and breathing is the basic sign that something is alive.

clue.text: People defending popular dramatist

indicators.note: the outer word surrounds and so guards the inner one, as defenders encircle what they protect

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A crowd of people stands up for a much-loved playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Racine was the great seventeenth-century French tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Racine wrote classical French tragedies such as Phèdre, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Wet coats left, muddy

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other like a coat around a body

parts.note: wet in the sense of feeble or sentimental means soppy

explanation.surface: Wet coats have been left looking a muddy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' reads as describing the coats, but it is a synonym for SOPPY, which 'coats' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is sloppy is wet and slushy underfoot, much like muddy ground.

clue.text: Towards the centre, fold up

parts.note: in as an adverb means inwards, towards the centre
a crease is a fold line

explanation.surface: An instruction to fold something up towards the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, 'up', used as a verb, as in upping the price.
explanation.definitionFit: To up a price or offer is to raise it, which is to increase it.

clue.text: Love child maybe painful to bring up

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing a word up means writing it from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: An illegitimate child might be a sore subject to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love child' suggests a child born outside marriage; here it is the child of the love goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, the Greek god of desire, was the son of Aphrodite, goddess of love.

clue.text: Land at home east of boat at sea

indicators.note: in an across clue east of means placed to the right, so this piece comes after
a thing at sea is confused, so the letters of boat are mixed up

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A boat at sea comes to land east of home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in landing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To land something, such as a contract, is to secure or get it.

clue.text: Fairly colourful glow around India

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a blush is a rosy glow on the cheeks
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A colourful glow is spreading around India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Fairly colourful': the -ish ending means somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bluish is somewhat blue, so it has a fair amount of one colour.

clue.text: Records from chief composer

parts.note: arch as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop
Charles Ives was an American composer

explanation.surface: Documents taken from the papers of a leading composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents and records kept for reference.

clue.text: Turkish commander breaking out? This has happened before!

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: out means not in
an aga was an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: An Ottoman general escapes from captivity, and it is not the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is read as the phrase it stands for, which the commander splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Groaning 'not again!' is the weary exclamation when something repeats itself.

clue.text: Dog food at the double?

definitions.meaning: chow is slang for food, so food doubled gives the same word twice

explanation.surface: Dog food served up fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the double' usually means quickly; here it doubles the word for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Greek character: shift for capital

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
scat, as a command, means go away or shift

explanation.surface: A Greek man has to move to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of Oman.

clue.text: Little time free for officer abroad

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: An officer serving overseas has a moment off.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, an officer in Canada.

clue.text: Relative number initially cut, that's a weight off my shoulders!

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, cut from the start

parts.note: one is a number

parts.words: that's a weight off my shoulders!
parts.note: phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: A relative, given a lower figure, breathes a sigh of relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially cut' removes the O of ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, a family relation.

clue.text: Stolen by gang, oven hot!

indicators.note: what is stolen is taken inside, so the oven sits within the gang

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: A gang has nicked a red-hot oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting weather is extremely hot weather.

clue.text: Fool breaking game?

definitions.meaning: a cue game in which players make breaks; the question mark flags the play on breaking

explanation.surface: A clown spoiling the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue sport scored in breaks, and to snooker someone is to trap or trick them.

clue.text: Trimmed, basic figure idiotic

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the ends, leaving the inner letters of the word basic

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Cutting things back to a basic figure is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as stupid as an ass, foolish.

clue.text: Queen guarded by good fairy

indicators.note: what is guarded sits inside its guard

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen protected by a kindly fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy-like spirit in Persian mythology.

clue.text: Stuff still on top of an Asian fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue being on top of means coming before the next piece

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
but means still, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Fill up still more with an exotic fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rambutan is a red, hairy-skinned tropical fruit from Southeast Asia, related to the lychee.

clue.text: Wine after month in effect contaminated

indicators.note: the wine comes after the rest in the answer
one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to do something is to effect it
Oct is short for October
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Wine that has gone off after a month is in effect spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in effect' reads as a phrase meaning virtually; split it, so 'in' places the month inside a verb meaning effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctored food or drink has been tampered with, often by adding something harmful.

clue.text: Finance worker shot

parts.note: to back a venture is to fund or finance it
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A banker or other finance employee is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like an adjective meaning worn out; it is a tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a stroke in tennis and similar sports played with the back of the hand facing forward.

clue.text: Some nerve heading off old raider!

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: the Saxons were invaders of early Britain

explanation.surface: An old invader showing real nerve as he sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell, so part of a nerve.

clue.text: Currency as it happens almost pinched by swine

indicators.note: what is pinched is held inside

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: the word is nearly complete, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: Cash being nicked by some swine in real time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' looks like a filler phrase; it describes a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolívar is the monetary unit of Venezuela.

clue.text: Sports official eating whopper for charity

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a ref is a referee
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A referee scoffs a burger at a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whopper' suggests a burger; it is a big lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is aid given to people in need, which is charity.

clue.text: Mark puts the kettle on, we hear

indicators.note: flags that the word is to be heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: someone who puts the kettle on brews tea

explanation.surface: Mark is making the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is a bruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is a dark mark on the skin left by a blow.

clue.text: Throw cakes without topping down

indicators.note: in a down clue the topping is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: buns are small cakes
to down food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Chuck away cakes without icing, then wolf them down.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that throws its rider unseats them.

clue.text: Spare kept in sack, poked nose in

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
other, as in the other one, means the spare one

explanation.surface: Someone nosy rummages in a sack for a spare.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bothered with something is to have taken trouble over it, involving oneself in it.

clue.text: Risk breaks, one in Chamonix — on this?

indicators.note: the word breaks apart and its letters are rebuilt

parts.note: un is French for one, and Chamonix is a French ski resort

explanation.surface: Taking a chance at a French ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'on this?' leans on the whole clue: one in Chamonix might ski on this.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a marked slope down which skiers travel at a resort such as Chamonix.

clue.text: Coat covering old pair of braces

indicators.note: the outer piece covers the inner, enclosing it

parts.note: fur is an animal's coat

explanation.surface: A coat over a worn pair of trouser braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'braces' suggests trouser straps; a brace is a pair, so two braces are four.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace means two, as in a brace of pheasants, so a pair of braces makes four.

clue.text: From behind, hold down and grind vegetable

indicators.note: reading from behind means reading backwards

parts.note: to pin someone is to hold them down
a rut, like a daily grind, is a dull routine

explanation.surface: Pinning something down from behind and grinding a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable.

clue.text: Play around, with puzzling one's aim

indicators.note: puzzling suggests confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fooling around while baffling people about your intentions.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to pursue many casual affairs with women, to sleep around.

clue.text: Absolutely not getting lift, crash

parts.note: no is a flat refusal
to doff a hat is to lift it in greeting

explanation.surface: Absolutely no lift is available after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' suggests a collision; it is slang for falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash, informally, is to fall asleep quickly, to doze off.

clue.text: Present banking pass for bank

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside, as a bank holds deposits

parts.note: to grant is to give or present
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A financial gift being deposited to pass to a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' and 'bank' look financial; the second is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a slope, and a gradient is the slope of a road or hill.
